title: Quick sweep micro-dashboard (personal) - Alex C.
content:
Goal: quick personal sweep to compare tiny config tweaks that affect p50/p90 and cost per 1M tokens. Use this as my one-page quick-decide sheet before I open a formal run in /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml.

Notes to self:
- keep runs < 15 mins each (short prompt seeds, 3 seeds/run)
- use deterministic prompt set: small-chat-10 (seeded), long-doc-3, code-query-4
- label experiment name with date and short tag (e.g. 2026-03-11--dynB_v_fixB)
- push promising configs to bench PR with plots and p95 cost delta

COMMANDS (local harness):
- ./run_micro_bench --model llama-70b-q4 --batching dynamic --batch_size_max 8 --seq 2048 --seedset small-chat-10
- ./cost_calc.py --tokens 1e6 --gpu_cost 2.4 --avg_throughput 12000

Quick table (CSV-style):
run_id,date,model,quant,batching,batch_max,seq_len,tokens_gen,avg_lat_ms,p90_lat_ms,cost_per_1M_usd,notes
R-260311-01,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,dynamic,8,512,120k,18.2,34.5,4.8,baseline dynamic batching small seqs
R-260311-02,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,fixed,4,512,118k,22.7,41.9,5.2,fixed batch smaller concurrency hurts p50 but p90 similar
R-260311-03,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,dynamic,16,512,122k,19.5,36.0,4.6,larger max batch helps throughput, slight p50 up
R-260311-04,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q8,q8,dynamic,8,512,121k,20.1,37.8,3.6,q8 shows good cost drop, p90 ~+3ms
R-260311-05,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,dynamic,8,2048,95k,45.8,102.3,6.1,longer seq increases tail a lot (KV cache pressure)
R-260311-06,2026-03-11,open-psi-13b,q4,dynamic,8,512,300k,9.4,18.0,2.1,cheap small model baseline for comparison
R-260311-07,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,dynamic,4,1024,110k,30.9,68.2,5.6,lower max batch reduces tail but increases cost
R-260311-08,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,fixed,8,512,119k,21.9,40.1,5.0,fixed with same max batch vs dynamic
R-260311-09,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-quantmix,qmix,dynamic,8,512,121k,19.8,35.9,3.9,quant-mix blend shows middle ground
R-260311-10,2026-03-11,redwood-70b-q4,q4,dynamic,8,256,140k,12.6,24.2,4.2,shorter seq improves tail and cost

Quick observations:
- For 512 seq, dynamic batching with batch_max 8 seems best p50/cost tradeoff for our workload.
- p90 is sensitive to long-seq runs (2048) and to max batch being high when many concurrent long requests hit KV cache (see R-260311-05).
- q8 (R-260311-04) reduces cost significantly; quality checks needed but latency impact small. Consider run-level quality eval on small prompt set.
- Small model (13b) gives clear cost win but accuracy mismatch for prod; use as fallback tier.

Quick calculations (notes):
- rough cost per 1M tokens = (gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_hour) * 1e6
  example: gpu $2.4/hr; throughput 12000 tok/s => 43.2M tok/hr => cost = 2.4 / 43.2 ~ $0.055 per 1M. Adjusted for overhead in infra => multiply by 1.1 => $0.061
- my sheet numbers use per-request observed throughput (includes client overhead) so final cost numbers are slightly higher than kernel-only calc.

Outstanding TODOs:
- [ ] run deterministic quality eval (small prompt set) for R-260311-04 (q8) and R-260311-09 (qmix) before proposing rollout
- [ ] test dynamic batching with early-flush (drop small tails) to see p90 effect
- [ ] add p99 capture for long-seq runs (automate trace sampling)
- [ ] push top-3 configs into bench PR with plots (link above)

Scratchpad (notes to self / quick logs):
- 11:03 started R-260311-01; env: dev-gpu-a, python 3.11, harness v0.9.1
- 11:15 noticed one jitter spike (GC event on node) — mark run as noisy? Keep but tag noisy
- 11:22 re-ran fixed batch variant to confirm numbers (R-260311-02)

Quick links for follow-up:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/112
- Example run traces (local): /tmp/microtraces/260311/*
- Slack thread: #bench-quick for live notes

Bottom line (1-liner): dynamic batching (batch_max 8) + q8/quanmix looks promising for short-to-medium seq production; need quick quality pass then escalate to formal dedicated-run matrix.

Sign-off: Alex C. (personal tracker)
